clue.text: Urge use of force

definitions.meaning: an irresistible inner drive or craving to do something
coercion, making someone act against their will

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a psychological drive one cannot resist, and the act of coercing someone by pressure.

clue.text: What one might get in bed is cause of infatuation

definitions.text: What one might get in bed
definitions.meaning: a garden flower, Catananche, grown in a flower bed
the arrow of the god of love that makes someone fall in love

explanation.walkthrough: 'in bed' suggests romance, but the bed is a flower bed: the plant Catananche has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman love god's arrow makes its victim smitten; the same name is given to a blue-flowered garden plant.

clue.text: Keener to jog more and run around inside

indicators.note: the jumbled run goes within the jumbled more
jogging shakes things up, so the letters of more are jumbled
the letters of run are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An eager runner wants to jog more and run about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keener' looks like a comparative of keen, but it is a noun: one who keens, or wails, at a funeral. Both 'to jog' and 'around' are anagram signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A keener is a person who wails in lament for the dead, as at an Irish funeral.

clue.text: A French sort of crepe left an impression unlike anything else

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: sort as a verb, rearranging these letters

parts.note: dented means left a dent, an impression

explanation.surface: A French pancake that made a lasting mark like no other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges CREPE to PRECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without precedent has never happened before, so it is like nothing else.

clue.text: Couple holding hands outside court pass out

indicators.note: the bridge pair sits either side of the word for court

parts.note: South and North are partners at bridge, a couple each holding a hand of cards
to woo is to court romantically

explanation.surface: Lovers hand in hand faint outside a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the players North and South partner each other, so a pair holding hands of cards gives S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, losing consciousness, often from strong emotion.

clue.text: You'll find salesperson's laughter somewhat offensive

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: A salesperson's laugh can be rather rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective meaning rude; it is a noun, a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce attack, and an offensive is a military assault.

clue.text: Reveal pretence

definitions.meaning: to display or put on view
an outward display put on to deceive, as in 'it was all for appearances'

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means display; as a noun it is a false outward appearance, as in 'just for effect'.

clue.text: It controls shock in heart transplants

indicators.note: transplanting moves things to new places, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Something that regulates trauma during heart transplant surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests a medical crisis; here it is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine net worn over the head holds a mass, or shock, of hair in place.

clue.text: Need husband not to start putting on weight

indicators.note: the abbreviation for weight puts on the trimmed husband like a garment, wrapping round it
the husband's word loses its opening letter

parts.note: man as in man and wife

explanation.surface: A husband needn't begin to put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting on' works like wearing clothes: the weight abbreviation wraps round the trimmed husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to need or lack it, as in 'the house wants painting'.

clue.text: Quietly put up with bearing additional weight

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to lump it is to put up with something unwelcome

explanation.surface: Someone silently tolerates carrying an extra load.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump describes a person carrying a little more weight than average, rounded or chubby.

clue.text: Complex situation doesn't require judge sitting in court

indicators.note: something not required is left out, so the judge's letter is dropped from the word for situation

parts.note: a job is a situation, a post of employment
a court sits in session

explanation.surface: A tricky case where no judge needs to preside over the court's hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like an adjective describing the situation, but it is a noun and the definition, in the psychological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology a complex is a fixation or preoccupation that dominates the mind, the same as a fixation.

clue.text: What one might assume when promoting snack food

definitions.text: What one might assume when promoting

parts.note: a sandwich is a snack
board is food or meals, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Something one takes on to advertise a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assume' means put on: an advertiser wears the pair of boards hung front and back.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of hinged placards worn over the shoulders lets a person walk around advertising something.

clue.text: Waste a lot of time in prison

parts.note: dung is animal waste, manure
an eon is an immensely long period of time

explanation.surface: Wasting years behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground cell for holding prisoners, especially in a castle.

clue.text: It blocks the sun after start of daybreak

indicators.note: we take only what comes after the first letter of the synonym for daybreak, so its opening letter goes

parts.note: dawning is daybreak, the first light of day

explanation.surface: Something shades us once morning has begun.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas canopy over a window or shopfront that gives shade from the sun.

clue.text: Disheartened suitor ends life, abandoned and alone

indicators.note: abandoned as in wild and unrestrained, so the letters are scrambled
losing its heart leaves only the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dejected lover takes his own life, deserted and solitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' empties suitor to SR; 'abandoned' scrambles SR with ENDSLIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no companions or allies leaves a person isolated and on their own.

clue.text: Creating gloom as shocking constraint is imposed on understanding

indicators.note: the word for understanding is hemmed in, confined within the word for shocking

parts.note: daring as in a daring, shocking outfit
ken is knowledge or understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: A shocking restriction on knowledge casts a pall.
explanation.definitionFit: To darken something is to make it gloomier, so darkening is the act of bringing gloom.

clue.text: Beat a Romanian up to protect loved one

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the words shelter the answer within them

explanation.surface: Assaulting a man from Romania to defend a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the letters run inside 'Beat a Romanian'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman with whom one is in love, a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Bowdlerise adventure story without craft

indicators.note: the craft is taken away from the title of the story

parts.note: Watership Down is Richard Adams's adventure novel about a band of rabbits
a ship is a craft, a vessel

explanation.surface: Censoring an adventure tale by cutting out the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Watership Down, Richard Adams's 1972 novel about rabbits, loses SHIP from its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowdlerising a text means censoring it, removing anything offensive, which weakens or dilutes it.

clue.text: Frost said this contributed to his art

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word for frost is heard as another word

parts.note: rime is hoar frost, ice crystals on surfaces

explanation.surface: A quote from the poet Robert Frost about his craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' seems to be the poet named in the surface, but it is the weather, rime, which sounds like the answer; the definition then refers back to Robert Frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Frost was a poet who wrote in traditional verse forms, so matching line-end sounds were part of his art.

clue.text: Squint returns, encapsulating your endlessly irritating verbal tic

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the trimmed pronoun inside it
returning means the word for squint is read backwards

parts.note: wonky means askew, squint

indicators.note: losing both ends leaves only the middle letters

explanation.surface: A recurring squint accompanies your annoying spoken habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squint' is an adjective here, meaning askew, not the act of narrowing the eyes; the reversal leaves room after its first letter for the trimmed pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Filler phrases dropped into speech without meaning are a common habit that grates on listeners.

clue.text: Lorry he's permitted to enter plant

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large truck

indicators.note: the word for permitted goes into the pronoun

parts.note: he, with 's as a link meaning 'is'
OK means allowed, permitted

explanation.surface: A lorry driver is allowed into a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTIC, short for articulated lorry, is a British term for a large truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower heads are eaten.

clue.text: On strike over position in regional office?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed above another

parts.note: out as in workers out on strike
a post is a position or job

explanation.surface: A strike over a job at a regional office.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: a remote station is literally office in a region.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote station or settlement, a branch office far from headquarters.

clue.text: Precisely tilts to move ball to the right

indicators.note: the round letter is lifted out of the word for tilts and placed elsewhere
in an across answer the right is the end, so the letter shifts to the finish

parts.note: to tilt is to joust, charge with a lance
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A knight's charges shift his ball to the right with exactness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move ball to the right' takes the O from JOUSTS and puts it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Just so means exactly right, arranged precisely as it should be.

clue.text: Boring part in document's charged account

indicators.note: the drill part is placed inside the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a bit is the part of a drill that bores

explanation.surface: A dull section of a legal paper relates to a charged account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests dull, but it means drilling: a bit is the cutting part of a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: When an account is debited, a sum is charged against it, taken out of the balance.

clue.text: Old-fashioned saw

definitions.meaning: out of date, no longer in style
past tense of see, as in going out with someone romantically

explanation.definitionFit: Both work: something that looks behind the times, and having gone out with someone, been seeing them.

clue.text: Bill's about to live in a comfortable position

indicators.note: the bill goes around the verb

parts.note: ad is an advertisement, a bill or poster
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A bill is due for someone to live comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in bed is a cosy, restful position.

clue.text: Instruction to pay off rank bad business publication

indicators.note: off as in gone bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, the British business newspaper

explanation.surface: A payment order settles the debts of a shoddy business magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker's draft is an order drawn on a bank, directing it to pay a sum to someone.

clue.text: Party backs leader in approving faith-based teaching and worship

indicators.note: the party follows behind, backing up the leading letter
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a do is a party
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: A political party supports a leader who approves of religious schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to worship, venerate or love intensely.

clue.text: See 17
Sweet-sounding fruit, from which one is picked

indicators.note: the word for a sweet is heard, not spelt

parts.note: candy is a sweet, confectionery
dates are fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: A tasty-sounding fruit that one picks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked' suggests fruit picking but the definition means selected, as from a shortlist.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates are the field of contenders for a post, from whom one is chosen or elected.
